In [[complex dynamics]], the '''[[Bifurcation theory|bifurcation]] [[Locus (mathematics)|locus]]''' of a parameterized family of one-variable [[holomorphic function]]s informally is a [[Locus (mathematics)|locus]] of those parameterized points for which the dynamical behavior changes drastically under a small perturbation of the parameter. Thus the bifurcation locus can be thought of as an analog of the [[Julia set]] in parameter space. Without doubt, the most famous example of a [[Bifurcation theory|bifurcation]] [[Locus (mathematics)|locus]] is the boundary of the [[Mandelbrot set]].

Parameters in the complement of the bifurcation locus are called '''[[J-stable]]'''.

* [[Mikhail Lyubich|Mikhail Yu. Lyubich]], ''Some typical properties of the dynamics of rational mappings (Russian)'', Uspekhi Mat. Nauk 38 (1983), no. 5(233), 197&ndash;198.
* [[Ricardo Mañé]], Paulo Sad and [[Dennis Sullivan]], ''On the dynamics of rational maps'', Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup. (4)  16  (1983),  no. 2, 193&ndash;217, http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1983_4_16_2_193_0. 
* [[Curtis McMullen|Curtis T. McMullen]], ''Complex dynamics and renormalization'', Annals of Mathematics Studies, 135, Princeton University Press, Princeton, NJ, 1994. {{ISBN|0-691-02982-2}}.
